title: A shipped Lua rule of the kbingest pattern table is quadratic on a hostile line, and the in-process mapper has no timeout
goal: kbingest's pattern-row guard refuses a rules row whose adjacent quantifiers overlap; the shipped Lua def rule takes under 0.5 ms on a 990-letter hostile line and still names the function of function f(, function M.f( and function M:f(; PatternMapper stops reading a file after PATTERN_FILE_TIMEOUT_S seconds and notes it; PATTERN_FILE_TIMEOUT_S is 10 and PatternMapper reads it when it maps a file

run:
import re, time
rx = re.compile(r'^\s*function\s+[\w.:]*?(?P<name>\w+)\s*\(')
line = 'function ' + 'a' * 990
t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(50):
    rx.search(line)
per = (time.perf_counter() - t) / 50 * 1000
assert per < 0.5, ('the Lua def rule takes %.2f ms on one hostile line' % per)

notes: Review G2 of SP-iir3d2tu: _tools/kbingest_rules.csv row 11, run by kbingest.py:1893-1905; nested_quantifier (kbingest.py:1721) misses adjacent quantifiers; MAP_TIMEOUT applies to processes only. ~4.5 ms per 990-letter line, ~2.5 h for MAP_MAX_FILES such 1 MB files. The repro uses the row's pattern literally; the fix may change the row.
